cases.say: a link's address ends at a space or a tab (the title is dropped) and escapes are undone
a link's title is its address normalised: scheme and host lower-cased, the host as punycode (an IDN look-alike shows as xn--)
links=https: an IDN host is still shown as punycode
rich text: a link's title is its address normalised too
rich text: a dropped element ends only at its own end tag
rich text: text after a nested list stays after it, in order and apart
rich text: a dropped element nested in itself ends at its own end tag, not the inner one
rich text: an end tag inside a comment, an attribute value, a bogus comment, CDATA or a nested text element does not end a dropped element
rich text: inside <!-- a nested <script> needs its own </script>, and a quoted > does not end an end tag
a link's address ends at a space, a tab or a line break (CommonMark); other whitespace is part of it and another control character spoils it, so the link is refused, not cut short
a mailto link's title shows each domain as a web host is shown (an IDN look-alike as punycode); a domain the URL parser rejects is refused; tel is as written
a web address's port must be a number up to 65535 (an empty port is allowed); anything else is refused
rich text: comments, a doctype and other bogus comments are read as a browser reads them, so none shows and none hides what follows
rich text: a tag name and a tag's end are read as a browser reads them: <svg-x> is not <svg>, <svg/> is empty, and only HTML whitespace separates attributes
rich text: a self-closing svg or math element is closed, so the text after it shows
rich text: a self-closing slash on an HTML element is ignored, as a browser ignores it, so an iframe or textarea drops to its end tag
rich text: a list placed directly in a list (as Google Docs and Word paste it) nests under the item before it
